endorsements.quote: Furthermore, many developing countries are still new to the use of AI in health research, and research ethicists need to catch up with what AI is, what it is not, what it can do, and what it can’t do.
We recommend future research on the implementation of thematic domains described in the guide and training of ethics committees on the key considerations for ethical review of AI research protocols.
The validation may involve testing AI tools on large, diverse, and representative datasets to ensure their accuracy, reliability, and fair benefit-sharing across populations [ 42 ].

To ensure inclusiveness and fairness, respondents emphasized the need to employ datasets that are inclusive and representative of the majority population that is likely to benefit from the AI tools to minimize potential biases as already discussed above.
Additionally, the research team should comprise of diverse disciplines, different age ranges with varying research experiences.

Therefore, research institutions, researchers and RECs should ensure that the research teams have strategies for collecting or accessing datasets that are adequate, relevant and necessary to address the research questions.
Additionally, research institutions should negotiate data sharing agreements (DSAs) that bind both provider and recipient scientists from inappropriate access and use of individuals’ data.
In addition, RECs should ensure that the datasets used in the development of AI tools for health research are anonymized.
It is important that the roles and responsibilities of the teams designing, deploying and using the AI systems are clearly defined [ 56 ].
Therefore, RECs may need to evaluate whether the AI innovations allow for human oversight in decision-making.
Despite these challenges, individuals who donate their clinical and research data reserve the right to decide on how their data may be used including future research and innovation purposes.
Therefore, RECs should ensure that researchers provide appropriate information on the applicable security measures to prevent possible harm to participants and end-users.
Regarding transparency and openness, researchers and developers ought to provide sufficient information on how the AI systems were built and should be used to cultivate trust and accountability.
The strategies should be reviewed by the REC to ensure that they respect participants and research communities’ values, interests and dignity.

unlisted_practices: Research ethics committees should use a structured guide with thematic questions when reviewing protocols for developing AI systems in health research.
Policy makers should develop contextualized national research guidelines for the development and deployment of AI in health research.
Researchers should clearly define the intended beneficiaries and how they will benefit from the AI tool.
Research institutions should provide mechanisms for oversight, redress, and regular auditing of AI systems.
Researchers should provide platforms to receive end-user questions and feedback and respond in a timely manner.
Developers should provide information about how AI works in simple language understandable to end-users regardless of education.
Research institutions should establish quality assurance standard operating procedures to ensure AI decisions are trustworthy.
Researchers should engage communities and stakeholders throughout AI tool development and describe how feedback is incorporated into design.
Researchers should plan for continuous evaluation and improvement of AI tools and engage government and non-government stakeholders for sustainability.
Developers should translate patient-facing AI tools into local languages.
Ethics committees should consider approving use of publicly available data without consent only when the research offers maximum societal benefit with minimal risk.

screen.reason: The paper develops a guide/framework for research ethics committees in Uganda reviewing AI health research based on a qualitative stakeholder study; its primary contribution is guidelines and recommendations for governance.
